title: Prism instrumentation targets (v1)
description: Projection of prism findings into sites a runtime harness should instrument. Produced by `prism targets`. Stable keys a consumer may diff on across runs and machines: targets[].id, site.{file,line,symbol}, kind, category, expected, source_algorithm, severity. Envelope fields a consumer must ignore when comparing documents: producer.{version,build_identity}, repo.root, repo.sha, diff.sha256. confidence/tier are stable for a given prism version and may change across versions as labeling improves. Bump schema_version on any breaking change.

schema_version.description: Targets contract version, currently 1.0. Every object is additionalProperties:false (closed world), so a document with schema_version 1.k validates ONLY against schema 1.k: consumers must validate with the schema matching the document's minor version. Minor bumps are backward-compatible in MEANING (existing fields keep their semantics; fields are only added) but not in closed-world validation. Breaking changes bump the major.

resolution_mode.description: The BUILD's dataflow-labeling capability (roadmap `--resolution`): nominal = DataFlow edges unlabeled (Phase 0); scoped = reaching-definitions labels; precise = external-index overlay. A different axis from targets[].confidence; no ordering relation between the two is defined.

algorithms.description: Algorithm names that were run to produce these targets, in run order.

build_identity.description: sha256 over the producing BINARY's own source inputs (prism's build.rs identity). Identical across repos and diffs; changes with every prism source change. Not a CPG/input identity.

root.description: Absolute repo root as seen by prism (informational; consumers must not rely on it).

sha.description: HEAD commit if the repo is a git checkout.

errors.description: Algorithms that were requested but failed; their findings are absent. Consumers must treat a non-empty list as partial coverage.

warnings.description: Non-fatal conditions the consumer must see: parse-quality warnings, files skipped at load time (unsupported language, unreadable), and projection warnings (dropped line-0 findings, dropped escaping paths, duplicate ids, unknown severities, omitted function bounds). A non-empty list means coverage is partial in the named way.

file.description: Repo-relative path, forward slashes. A producer drops (and records a warning for) any finding whose path is absolute or escapes the repo root, so consumers may rely on containment.

line.description: 1-indexed line of the finding anchor (the call / acquire / guard site).

symbol.description: Name of the innermost function enclosing `line` when the producer could determine it from the parsed file; otherwise the finding's own function name. When the two disagree the producer prefers the enclosing function and records a warning.

function_start_line.description: 1-indexed first line of the enclosing function. Producers that parsed the file MUST fill this and function_end_line whenever the enclosing function is found; the Python harness relies on the range to scope injection to this site (CR-1) and fails safe (no injection) when it is absent.

function_end_line.description: 1-indexed last line of the enclosing function (inclusive). See function_start_line.

id.description: Lowercase hex sha256 of the compact canonical JSON array [file, line, symbol_or_empty_string, source_algorithm, category, description, severity] (serde_json compact serialization of a 7-element array; no delimiter ambiguity). Distinct findings at one site get distinct ids; the same source and diff yield the same id across runs.

kind.description: What the harness should do at the site. external_call → inject faults on the callee; resource_* → watch acquire/release pairing; boundary → cross-module/service edge; contract → guard/postcondition to check; error_handler → handler that should be exercised; data_origin → provenance seed; other → informational.

category.description: Prism finding category string, verbatim (e.g. missing_error_handling, missing_counterpart); `uncategorized` when the finding carried none.

property.description: The property the finding claims may be violated; the harness reports whether runtime evidence confirms or refutes it.

callee.description: Callee text as written at the site (e.g. requests.post, os.open, db.Query).

counterpart.description: For resource kinds: the expected release/counterpart name (e.g. close, unlock).

source_algorithm.description: Prism algorithm name (echo, absence, contract, angle, provenance, membrane, delta, taint, ...).

confidence.description: Per-finding evidence-path label, mirroring prism's ResolutionConfidence plus `unlabeled`. exact: every edge on the evidence path is Exact and the algorithm is AST-only or fully labeled; nameonly: at least one name-only edge; unlabeled: the evidence path crosses edges prism cannot label yet (Phase 0: every CPG-derived finding, because DataFlow edges carry no confidence). This is a DIFFERENT AXIS from producer.resolution_mode.

tier.description: asserted iff confidence == exact AND the file's parse quality is clean. A claim about the EVIDENCE PATH, never about the truth of the heuristic the algorithm encodes. Candidates are still worth instrumenting — runtime confirmation is how a candidate becomes evidence.

severity.description: Prism severity, one of the four known values; a producer maps any unknown severity to `concern` and records a warning.

parse_quality.description: Worst parse quality over the finding's evidence-bearing files (anchor + related files) from prism's authoritative per-file map; `unknown` when a file's quality is not knowable (e.g. contract findings computed against an --old-repo tree) — unknown always yields tier candidate.
